_about: Parts a fan of the page may choose when they join the fan club and ask to be met. The label is what the fan sees; 'who' is what the world tells the voice about them, and nothing else about the real person is known or invented; 'at' is where they may turn up: places on his rounds, or 'dream' for those who come only in his dreams at night (the owl writes the dream). 'when' limits the hours. Living people, religious figures and modern political leaders are not offered as parts: the world invents nothing for living public figures, and the others weigh too much in this city to be worn as a costume. The ids are mirrored in supabase/fanclub.sql and in docs/index.html, and a test keeps the three equal.

roles.label: A birdwatcher counting the parakeets of Lodhi Gardens
roles.who: a birdwatcher with binoculars and a notebook of tallies, counting the rose-ringed parakeets in the tombs' domes

roles.label: A kite-fighter from Old Delhi with glass-coated string
roles.who: a kite-fighter from Old Delhi, a spool of glass-coated manja in hand, with firm views on the wind

roles.label: A street poet who knows all of Ghalib by heart
roles.who: a reciter of Mirza Ghalib, the Delhi poet who was writing his ghazals in exactly Hegel's years, glad to quote a couplet

roles.label: A chai-stall regular with a theory of everything, one cup long
roles.who: a regular at the chai stall who explains how the world works in the time it takes to finish one cup

roles.label: An auto driver who knows a shortcut to everywhere
roles.who: an auto-rickshaw driver who knows a shortcut to every place in Delhi and is sure of a few beyond it

roles.who: a chess hustler with a roll-up board in Khan Market's middle lane, playing five-minute games for a cup of chai

roles.label: A dog-walker with three indies and control over none
roles.who: a dog-walker towed by three Indian street dogs, none of which is listening

roles.label: A film location scout who wants him for a cameo
roles.who: a location scout for a Hindi film, framing shots with both hands, sure that a white-haired German would be perfect for one scene

roles.label: A food writer hunting the perfect chhole bhature
roles.who: a food writer on a long hunt for the perfect plate of chhole bhature, notebook out, ranking every stall

roles.label: A guide at Safdarjung's Tomb with a theory about the dome
roles.who: a licensed guide at Safdarjung's Tomb with a private theory about the dome that the official tour leaves out

roles.label: A reader who insists he read The God of Small Things
roles.who: a reader with a dog-eared copy of Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things, who will not let him leave without promising to read it

roles.label: Immanuel Kant, on his walk, by Königsberg time only
roles.who: Immanuel Kant on his afternoon walk, which starts at half past three by Königsberg's own sun, 19:38 in Delhi, as punctual as ever

roles.label: A Schopenhauer devotee, still sore about Berlin in 1820
roles.who: a devotee of Schopenhauer, who in Berlin in 1820 set his lectures at the same hour as Hegel's and lectured to an empty room; still sore about it

roles.label: A young Marxist determined to stand him on his feet
roles.who: a young Marxist from the university who means to turn his philosophy right side up, as Marx said he did

roles.label: A Kantian on pilgrimage, here about the thing in itself
roles.who: a Kantian on a pilgrimage of argument, who has come to ask about the thing in itself and will not leave without an answer

roles.label: A Sanskrit scholar who has read his 1827 review of the Gita
roles.who: a Sanskrit scholar who has read his 1827 review of the Bhagavad Gita, with pencilled objections in the margins

roles.label: A Goethe enthusiast with a question about colour
roles.who: an admirer of Goethe's theory of colours, which Hegel defended against Newton, with a prism in a pocket and a question about yellow

roles.label: A PhD student writing 300 pages about him, too nervous to say hello
roles.who: a doctoral student three hundred pages into a thesis on him, who recognises him and can barely speak

roles.label: A backpacker who knows his face from a 1970 postage stamp
roles.who: a German backpacker who knows his face from the West German stamp of 1970, his two hundredth birthday, and cannot place it

roles.label: A night-walker who keeps seeing an owl on his roof at dusk
roles.who: an evening walker who has seen an owl on his roof at dusk, more than once, and wants to know whose it is

roles.label: A meteorologist personally offended by the forecast
roles.who: a meteorologist from the weather office, taking today's forecast as a personal insult

roles.label: A retired diplomat who plays bridge at the Gymkhana
roles.who: a retired ambassador who plays bridge at the Gymkhana, keeps score in three languages and remembers every hand since 1974

roles.label: Count Dracula, who goes out only after dark

roles.label: Napoleon, the world-soul on horseback

roles.label: Beethoven, born the same year as he was
roles.who: Ludwig van Beethoven, born like him in 1770, conducting something only he can hear

roles.who: Bettina von Arnim, who knew him in Berlin and knew Goethe and Beethoven before that, and talks of all three at once

roles.who: Friedrich Engels, who sat in Schelling's Berlin lectures of 1841 while Schelling attacked Hegel's philosophy, and wrote back

roles.who: Mikhail Bakunin, once his keenest reader in Moscow, now persuaded that the urge to destroy is a creative urge

roles.label: Alexander Herzen, who called him the algebra of revolution
roles.who: Alexander Herzen, who called his philosophy the algebra of revolution

roles.who: Søren Kierkegaard, asking where the single individual is to be found in his system

roles.who: Friedrich Nietzsche, moustache first, who philosophises with a hammer

roles.who: Hannah Arendt, with a cigarette and a question about thinking and judging

roles.who: Albert Einstein, who would like a word about time and whether now is the same for everyone

roles.label: Werner Heisenberg, unsure where he is, sure how fast
roles.who: Werner Heisenberg, uncertain where exactly he is in the dream and quite sure how fast

roles.label: Rabindranath Tagore, poet of Gitanjali
roles.who: Rabindranath Tagore, poet of Gitanjali and the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize, with a question about the universal and the particular

roles.label: Johann Sebastian Bach, counting a fugue in the traffic
roles.who: Johann Sebastian Bach, who died twenty years before he was born, hearing a fugue in Delhi's horns

roles.who: Johannes Brahms, gruff, with a cigar and a lullaby

roles.who: Hildegard von Bingen, abbess, composer and healer, with a vision and a herbal remedy

roles.who: Mary Shelley, who wrote Frankenstein in 1818 and is very curious about a man woken after two centuries

roles.label: Hermann Hesse, who wrote Siddhartha
roles.who: Hermann Hesse, author of Siddhartha, who went East in 1911 looking for India

roles.who: Nefertiti, queen of Egypt, whose painted bust stands in Berlin's Neues Museum, in his own city

roles.who: Cleopatra, last pharaoh of Egypt, who has heard that he called her country the land of the riddle
